H1.allowed_claim: Random internal evaluation was consistently optimistic for QWK and severe-class recall, but not for Macro-F1 or all error metrics.
prohibited_claims: Random splitting uniformly overestimates future performance.
An interval crossing zero proves equivalence.
The descriptive gap is the causal effect of splitting.

H2.allowed_claim: LightGBM improved several metrics and passed the Macro-F1 rule, but substantially reduced fatal recall relative to weighted Logistic.
prohibited_claims: LightGBM is uniformly or safely superior to weighted Logistic.
Macro-F1 alone satisfies the joint incremental-value rule.

H3.reason: No frozen SHAP ranking or SHAP bootstrap interval exists yet.
H3.required_next_evidence: Spearman rank agreement between frozen random-test and temporal-test global SHAP importance, with its prespecified interval.

manuscript_positioning.primary_empirical_message: Evaluation-protocol optimism is metric dependent, with degradation in ordinal agreement and severe-class recall despite stable Macro-F1.
manuscript_positioning.secondary_empirical_message: Nonlinear-model gains depend on the metric and include a fatal-recall trade-off.
manuscript_positioning.scope: STATS19 2018-2024 and the frozen collision-time feature set
